[[File:Tuna Altınel.jpg|thumb|Tuna Altınel]]
'''Tuna Altınel''' is a Turkish [[mathematician]], born February 12, 1966, in [[Istanbul]], who has worked at the [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1|University Lyon 1]] in France since 1996.<ref name="CV">[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/~logicum/cvTunaAltinel.pdf ''Tuna Altınel, CV'']</ref> He is a specialist in [[group theory]] and [[mathematical logic]]. With [[Alexandre Borovik]] and [[Gregory Cherlin]], he proved a major case of the [[Stable group|Cherlin–Zilber conjecture]].<ref name="amsbook">{{cite book
|url= https://bookstore.ams.org/surv-145 
|title= Simple Groups of Finite Morley Rank 
|first1= Tuna|last1= Altinel
|first2= Alexandre|last2= Borovik|author2-link=Alexandre Borovik
|first3=Gregory|last3= Cherlin|author3-link=Gregory Cherlin
|date= 2008
|series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs
|volume=145
|publisher= [[American Mathematical Society]] 
|location=Providence, RI
}}; {{cite journal|url= https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2010-47-04/S0273-0979-10-01287-5/|title=Simple Groups of Finite Morley Rank (Book Review)|first=Dugald|last= Macpherson| authorlink=Dugald Macpherson| journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]| date=2010|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-10-01287-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Altınel is active in the [[Academics for Peace]] movement, which supports a peaceful resolution of the [[Kurdish-Turkish conflict|conflict in south-eastern Turkey]], and calls for the [[human rights]] of the civilian population to be respected.<ref name="Petition">[https://barisicinakademisyenler.net/node/63 Peace Petition: "We will not be parties to this crime!", Academics for Peace]</ref> Accused by the Turkish authorities of membership in a terrorist organization, Altınel has been imprisoned since May 11, 2019, at the [[Kepsut]] prison in Turkey.<ref>''[https://bianet.org/bianet/ifade-ozgurlugu/209220-tutuklu-akademisyen-tuna-altinel-in-ilk-durusmasi-30-temmuz-da  Article on Altınel's first hearing],'' on the [[Bianet]] website, June 10, 2019</ref>

==Education and career==

After undergraduate studies in mathematics and computer science at [[Boğaziçi University]], Istanbul, Altınel received his
[[doctorate]] from [[Rutgers University]] ([[New Jersey]], United States) under the direction of Gregory Cherlin.<ref>''[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=6253 Tuna Altınel]'', on the website [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]].</ref> In 1996 he joined the [[:fr:Institut Camille Jordan|department of mathematics]] of the university [[:fr:Université Claude-Bernard-Lyon-I|Lyon-1]], as [[:fr:Maître de conférences (France)|maître de conférences]], and completed his [[:fr:habilitation à diriger des recherches|French habilitation]] in 2001.<ref name="CV" />

Altınel has written 26 mathematical articles, principally on the subject of [[Group (mathematics)|groups]] in [[model theory]], more particularly groups of finite [[Morley rank]] and the 
[[Stable group#The Cherlin-Zilber Conjecture|Cherlin–Zilber Algebraicity Conjecture]], concerning the structure of the [[simple group]]s of finite Morley rank.  He is joint author with Alexandre Borovik and Gregory Cherlin of a book
in which this conjecture is proved in the case of infinite [[Rank of a group#Generalizations and related notions|2-rank]], after the development of a body of machinery analogous to certain chapters of finite simple group theory.<ref name="amsbook" />

Altınel's doctoral advisees include [[Éric Jaligot]], winner of the 2000 [[Association for Symbolic Logic#Sacks Prize|Sacks Prize]],<ref>[https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/sacks-prize-recipients/List List of Sacks Prize winners], on the Association for Symbolic Logic website.</ref> a prize given annually for an outstanding doctoral thesis in mathematical logic<ref>[https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/sacks-prize-recipients/sacks-prize-nominations-and-other-information/Sacks Sacks Prize conditions], on the Association for Symbolic Logic website.</ref> (doctoral thesis supervised jointly by Tuna Altınel and Bruno Poizat<ref>''[https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S107989861400002X In Memoriam: ÉRIC JALIGOT],'' Adrien Deloro, Bull. Symbolic Logic 20, pp.  103&ndash;104, March 2014</ref>). He is active in the domain of scientific cooperation with Turkey; in particular, he was an organizer of an international mathematics conference held in Istanbul in 2016 in honor of Alexandre Borovik and [[Ali Nesin]] ([[Leelavati Award|Leelavati prize]] winner, 2018).<ref>73 participants from 9 countries. [https://sites.google.com/site/bnpair2016/participants List of participants, BN-Pair Conference in honor of Alexandre Borovik and Ali Nesin]
</ref>

==Political activities==

===Overview===

Altınel has been an active supporter of a peaceful resolution of the conflict in southeastern Turkey and of human rights and civil liberties in Turkey.<ref name=Ahval />

With regard to the Kurdish conflict in southeastern Turkey,  he was one of 116 academics who signed a 2003 letter in support of a peaceful resolution of that conflict,<ref>[https://bianet.org/english/politics/17302-116-university-professors-call-for-peac "116 University professors call for peace"], Bianet website, March 13, 2003] (letter signed also by Füsün Üstel)</ref> among the first group of signatories of a similar peace petition in  January 2016 that garnered 1128 signatures at the time of its promulgation under the title "We will not be parties to this crime," <ref name="Petition and List" /> among the 132 intellectuals calling for assistance to those wounded in the conflict at [[Cizre]],<ref>[http://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/turkiye/473648/Aydinlar_ve_sanatcilardan_devlete_Cizre_cagrisi.html "Aydinlar_ve_sanatcilardan_devlete_Cizre_cagrisi.html "Intellectuals and artists call on the state on behalf of Cizre"], Cumhuriyet, February 1, 2016 (Turkish);
[http://m.bianet.org/english/human-rights/171725-we-are-ready-to-save-those-in-cizre-if-you-won-t "We are ready to save those in Cizre if you won't,"] Bianet website, February 2, 2016; 
[https://www.ihd.org.tr/cizrede-insanlik-oluyor/ Cizre’de İnsanlık Ölüyor! "(People are dying in Cizre!),"]  Human Rights Association, Turkey, February 1, 2016 (Turkish)
</ref> and one of 170 academics to sign a letter in 2018 opposing the Afrin operation.<ref>
''[http://www.akasyam.com/afrin-operasyonuna-hayir-diyen-170-kisilik-ihanet-listesi-158067/ "Afrin Operasyonuna hayır diyen 170 kişilik ihanet listesi! (The list of 170 traitors who say no to the Afrin Operation)," Akasyam News website, January 28, 2018]'',
''[https://bianet.org/english/law/203372-investigation-launched-against-signatories-of-afrin-letter "Investigation launched against signatories of Afrin Letter"]''</ref> On February 21, 2019, he acted as translator for a former member of parliament of the [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]] (HDP) at a public meeting in [[Lyon]], [[France]], in which a documentary on the Cizre massacres was shown, followed by a discussion.<ref name="February 21" />

With the resumption of active conflict in August 2015 following a period of relative calm, Altınel reached out to the affected community and began to visit the areas involved in September 2015.<ref name=Ahval>[https://ahvalnews.com/academics-peace/man-who-has-done-his-duty-land-and-peace  "A man who has done his duty for this land, and for peace," Nurcan Baysal, Ahval News website, June 25, 2019]; 
[https://ahvalnews.com/tr/baris-akademisyenleri/gozlerini-aklini-kalbini-kapatmayanlardan-biri-tuna-altinel ''Gözlerini, aklını, kalbini kapatmayanlardan biri: Tuna Altınel'' (One who does not shut his eyes, mind, or heart: Tuna Altınel), Nurcan Baysal, Ahval News website, June 18, 2019 (Turkish)]
"August 2015;" "September 2017;" "never stopped showing his support";
</ref> His own account of these activities is quoted below, from subsequent court testimony.

With the trials of the signatories of the January 2016 petition and the broader wave of repression following the attempted coup of July 2016, described in more detail below, questions of academic freedom and freedom of speech become more prominent. Altınel's actions in this direction include
* a petition responding to the suicide of Mehmet Fatih Traş, an academic fired for his involvement with the peace petition (February 2017)<ref>Among the first signatories: ''[https://www.liberation.fr/debats/2017/12/05/turquie-appel-pour-la-liberte-des-universitaires_1614618 "Turquie : appel pour la liberté des universitaires (Turkey: a petition for academic freedom)", Liberation, December 5, 2017]''; 
''[http://www.kedistan.net/2017/03/01/petition-universitaires-2017/ "Universitaires pour la Paix • Une pétition à diffuser (Academics for Peace: a petition to be circulated," Kedistan website, March 1, 2017]'';
''[http://www.kedistan.net/2017/02/26/mehmet-fatih-tras-suicide-regime-turc/, "Mehmet Fatih Traş suicidé par le régime turc (Mehmet Fatih Traş suicided by the Turkish regime)," Kedistan website, February 26, 2017]''  
</ref>
* denunciation of the role of the Turkish research council [[TÜBİTAK]] in the state of emergency following the attempted coup d'état of 2016 (April 2017); the [[CNRS]] Scientific Council voted unanimously to recommend to the CNRS to reconsider its agreements concerning collaboration with TÜBİTAK (April 24–25, 2017).<ref>
[https://blogs.mediapart.fr/les-invites-de-mediapart/blog/170417/tuebitak-organisme-scientifique-ou-outil-politique "Tübitak: organisme scientifique ou outil politique? (Tübitak: scientific organization or political instrument?)]", Mediapart, April 17, 2017 (French). "This appeal by the Turkish mathematician Tuna Altınel ...";
[https://www.cnrs.fr/comitenational/cs/recommandations/24-25_avril_2017/Reco__Relations_avec_le_TUBITAK.pdf "Recommandation: Les relations avec le Conseil de la recherche scientifique et technique de Turquie (TÜBİTAK)" (Recommendation: Relations with the scientific and technical research council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK))],  CNRS Scientific Council, April 24--25, 2017</ref>
* publication of a review article on the trials of the Academics for Peace entitled "Les procès contre les Universitaires pour la paix : extraits d’une comédie politico-juridique (The trials of the Academics for Peace: scenes from a politico-juridical spectacle)".<ref>
Tuna Altınel, "Les procès contre les Universitaires pour la paix : extraits d’une comédie politico-juridique (The trials of the Academics for Peace: scenes from a politico-juridical spectacle)", chapter in 
[https://univ-droit.fr/recherche/actualites-de-la-recherche/parutions/27197-liberte-s-en-turquie-en-mediterranee Table of Contents, "Liberté(s)! En Turquie ? En Méditerranée ! (Freedom(s)! In Turkey? In the Mediterranean!"]), Mathieu Touzeil-Divina, L'Epitoge, June 2018, Revue Méditerrqanéenne de Droit Public Vol. 9, {{ISBN|979-1-0926-8433-9}}, Part I: ''Freedom(s) of speech for our Turkish colleagues!''</ref>
* petition in support of Academic for Peace Füsün Üstel<ref>One of first 63 signatories; Entry by Igor Babou on seenthis.net, cached at ''[https://seenthis.net/tag/f%25C3%25BCsun_%25C3%25BCstel]''</ref>

These activities have led to two separate court cases against Altınel in Turkey and his social media postings have been used to justify the second of these cases.<ref>''[https://www.iha.com.tr/haber-pkk-propagandasi-yapan-akademisyen-tutuklandi-779668/ "PKK propagandası yapan akademisyen tutuklandı (Academic who made propaganda for the PKK arrested)" IHA, May 11, 2019 (Turkish)]'': "sosyal medya araştırmasında" (investigation of social media)</ref>

===January 2016 petition and Academics for Peace===

Altınel was one of the first signatories of the January 2016 peace petition entitled "We will not be parties to this crime!", which was promulgated by the Academics for Peace on January 11, 2016.<ref name="Petition and List">''[https://barisicinakademisyenler.net/node/63 Text of the petition "We will not be parties to this crime:, Website of the Academics for Peace]'';
''[https://www.kamusaati.com/turkiye-haberleri/1128-akademisyenden-devleti-suclayan-skandal-bildiriye-imza-h4306.html  list of the first 1128 signatories of the petition (one missing: accessed June 20, 2019)]'' (Turkish)</ref>

The following day, President [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan|Erdoğan]] publicly criticized the signatories, and within a few days 27 had been arrested."<ref>[[Presidency of Recep Tayyip Erdoğan#State of emergency and purges|President Erdoğan: State of Emergency]]: "terrorist propaganda", "darkest of people", "enemy of the state", "pit of treachery"; ''[https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2016/02/12/more-1000-turkish-scholars-are-under-criminal-investigation-signing-petition "Turkish Academe Under Attack," Elizabeth Redden, Inside Higher Ed, February 12, 2016]'': "treason"
''[https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/jan/14/turkish-prosecutors-investigate-academics-criticised-erdogan-petition Turkish prosecutors to investigate academics over Erdoğan petition, Guardian news site, January 14, 2019]'': "treason", "fifth columns"
</ref> At the same time foreign reaction was strongly supportive of the signatories.<ref>
''[https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2016/02/12/more-1000-turkish-scholars-are-under-criminal-investigation-signing-petition "Turkish Academe Under Attack," Elizabeth Redden, Inside Higher Ed, February 12, 2016]'': "chilling effect", "extremely worrying", "dismayed ... grave concern; [[:fr:Universitaires pour la paix#Réactions étrangères face à la répression|Academics for peace: Foreign reactions]] (French): U.S. Ambassador, Germany, professional associations, international associations, PEN, etc.</ref>

The peace petition ultimately garnered 2212 signatures of academics, largely in Turkey.<ref name="Petition" /> Altınel is one of over 750 signatories from the first group of 1128 such who
have been prosecuted or sentenced as individuals for that act under Turkish Anti-Terrorism legislation, through June 2019,<ref>''[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vT05GTWUQMDot1iPfMsieJsWLGBorbNlJyLP5IdtvJVEcKRw8C8qMxFXPighYZkz7pf2ENP2bXZ3DMo/pubhtml?gid=1873917137  Academics for Peace&mdash;Hearing Statistics],'' accessed June 19, 2019</ref> on a charge of "propaganda in support of a terrorist organization."  Since 2016 Altınel has been an active
and vocal supporter both of the content of this petition and of the civil rights of its signers.

In the second hearing in his case, February 28, 2019, at the 29th Central Criminal Court, Çağlayan Courthouse, [[Istanbul]], Altınel testified that he had aided civilian victims of military operations that took place in the towns placed under military curfew:<ref name="Feb28">''[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/SoutienTunaAltinel/doc/19_02_28_Defense/ADefense20_EN_notes.pdf Translation of statement by Altınel, Feb. 28, 2019]''</ref>

{{Blockquote|text=Since September 2015, I have traveled several times to a number of provinces, including some of those mentioned in the Peace Petition which I signed. ...  I carried bag upon bag of provisions to help the victims of destruction and forced migration, I spoke with those who had lost their homes and relatives. I did all of this on my own initiative, and my principle was as follows: If every Turkish citizen will do what I do, we will come closer to peace.

You can find the traces of my efforts where I sojourned in the towns of [[Sur, Diyarbakır|Sur]], [[Nusaybin]], [[Cizre]], [[Hakkâri (city)|Hakkari]], and [[Yüksekova]].  The Prosecutor may use this as evidence against me. ...  I did not simply sign the Peace Petition. I thought about it, felt it, lived it.  I wrote that text.<ref>This sentence follows one that is obviously metaphorical; it may be intended in the same spirit.</ref>  I stand behind every sentence.}}

The sentencing hearing for Altınel's trial for "propaganda on behalf of a terrorist organization" in the context of the Academics for Peace Trials is scheduled for July 16, 2019.<ref>''[https://www.lyoncapitale.fr/justice/lyon-tuna-altinel-le-mathematicien-arrete-en-turquie-juge-en-juillet/ Lyon: Tuna Altinel, the mathematician arrested en Turkey, judged in July, Justin Boche, Lyon Capitale, June 10, 2019]'' (French)</ref>

===2019 charge and imprisonment===

On April 12, 2019, on arriving for a visit to Turkey, Altınel's passport was confiscated at the airport.  On May 10 he requested a new passport at the [[Balıkesir]] prefecture and was taken into custody for interrogation and placed in pre-trial detention on the following day. It was learned later that a new charge had been filed against him on April 30, 2019, at the prosecutor general's office in Balıkesir.<ref>''[http://www.balikesirhaberajansi.com/haber-30038-pkk-konferansinda-konusmayi-tercume-eden-akademisyen-balikesirde-yakalandi-ve-tutuklandi.html Article: Academic who acted as translator at PKK {{bracket|sic}} conference captured and arrested], Balıkesir Press Agency, May 11, 2019'' (Turkish)</ref>

This new charge is "membership in a terrorist organization",<ref>Either the [PKK] or the legally registered Lyon Society of Kurds; not specified in published legal documents</ref>
based on his participation on February 21, 2019, at a public meeting in [[Villeurbanne]], near Lyon, France. This meeting was organized by the local Kurdish Society; a documentary was shown on the subject of the [[December 2015–February 2016 Cizre curfew#Cizre basement massacre|Cizre massacres]] and a discussion was held with a former member of the Turkish parliament, [[Faysal Sarıyıldız]] (HDP), now in exile.{{refn|Parliamentary deputy from [[Şırnak Province|the province of Şırnak]] from 2011 to 2017, in [[:fr:Faysal Sarıyıldız#Exil|exile]] since 2016. 
After the resumption of the Turkish-Kurd conflict in summer 2015,<ref name="France24nov16">
''[https://observers.france24.com/fr/20161118-sirnak-ville-rasee-symbole-guerre-entre-turquie-kurdes "Sirnak, a city leveled, symbol of the war between Turkey and the Kurds"],'' on [[France 24]], November 18, 2016.</ref> 
and the [[December 2015–February 2016 Cizre curfew#Cizre basement massacre|December 2015 Cizre basement massacre]], 
accused by Erdoğan of transporting firearms intended for terrorists in his car,<ref name="Sabah190416">''[https://www.sabah.com.tr/gundem/2016/04/19/erdogan-unvani-milletvekili-ama-arabasinda-silah-tasiyor Statement by President Erdoğan regarding Faysal Sarıyıldız],'' reported in [[Sabah (newspaper)|the newspaper Sabah]], April 19, 2016. (Turkish)</ref>
a charge he has characterized as "an odious fabrication.".<ref name="humanite120716">''[https://www.humanite.fr/faysal-sariyildiz-letat-turc-impose-lenfer-aux-villes-kurdes-611751 Interview with Faysal Sarıyıldız],'' in L'Humanité, July 12, 2016; ''[https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/international/260816/avec-erdogan-le-risque-est-que-la-turquie-devienne-une-nouvelle-syrie Interview with Faysal Sarıyıldız],'' in [[Mediapart]], August 26, 2016. (Both in French)</ref> Honorary citizen of the town of [[Champigny-sur-Marne|Champigny-sur-Marne (94)]] and frequently [[:fr:Faysal Sarıyıldız#Honneurs et invitations|called on to discuss]] the conflict with the Kurds in Turkey and the Cizre basement massacres.}} At that public meeting, Altınel acted as translator for the former MP.<ref name="February 21">[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/SoutienTunaAltinel/doc/19_06_11VillaniLeDrian.pdf Cédric Villani, June 11, French National Assembly], in French with English translation.</ref>

On May 8 [[Füsun Üstel]] was incarcerated and began serving a 15-month sentence for signing the peace petition of January 2016. Altınel was arrested on May 11.<ref>''[http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/top-french-diplomat-due-in-turkey-for-bilateral-talks-144122 Turkey, France to discuss Syria, strained bilateral affairs]''</ref> After his first hearing on the new charge was scheduled for July 30, 2019, he was released.<ref>2nd Central Criminal Court in Balıkesir. [https://bianet.org/bianet/ifade-ozgurlugu/209220-tutuklu-akademisyen-tuna-altinel-in-ilk-durusmasi-30-temmuz-da "First hearing for an Academic for Peace"], Bianet website, June 10, 2019. (Turkish)</ref>

===Reactions===

====Press reports====

Altınel's May 11 arrest was widely reported in the press, notably in France and in Turkey.

Some early reports of the arrest in Turkey quoting variously from Altınel's lawyer or Academics for Peace put the case in the context of the Academics for Peace trials and the conference held in Lyon, France.<ref>[https://www.evrensel.net/haber/379190/baris-akademisyeni-tuna-altinel-tutuklandi "Barış Akademisyeni Tuna Altınel tutuklandı" (Academic for Peace Tuna Altinel Arrested), Evrensel, May 11, 2019], [http://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/turkiye/1387929/Baris_Akademisyeni_Tuna_Altinel_tutuklandi.html "Barış Akademisyeni Tuna Altınel tutuklandı" (Academic for Peace Tuna Altınel tutuklandı" (Academic for Peace Tuna Altinel Arrested), Cumhuriyet, May 11, 2019], [https://nupel.net/akademisyen-tuna-altinel-tutuklandi-22269h.html "Akademisyen Tuna Altinel tutuklandi" (Academic Tuna Altınel arrested), Nüpelö May 11, 2019]</ref> Other reports originating with the [[İhlas News Agency]] and reported on [[Habertürk]] and elsewhere described the case as the capture of a wanted terrorist; one of these reports stated that an anti-terrorist operation captured five members of [[Gülen movement|Gülen Movement]] and the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] (PKK), listing Altınel's arrest as the fifth.<ref>[https://www.haberturk.com/balikesir-haberleri/68993980-pkk-propagandasi-yapan-akademisyen-tutuklandi Arrest of an academic making propaganda for the PKK"], [[Habertürk]], May 11, 2019, Source: İHA;
[https://www.haberturk.com/balikesir-haberleri/68984359-balikesir-merkezli-feto-ve-pkkkck-operasyonu-5-kisi-yakalandi ''Balıkesir merkezli FETÖ ve PKK/KCK operasyonu: 5 kişi yakalandı'' (FETÖ PKK Operation Based in Balıkesır: 5 People Captured], May 11, 2019. Habertürk, May 11, 2019, Source: İHA.
(Turkish)</ref>

The first article in France, in [[Mediapart]],<ref>''[https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/international/110519/arrestation-en-turquie-d-un-mathematicien-de-l-universite-lyon-i?onglet=full Arrest of a Mathematician from the university Lyon-1 in Turkey]'' Mediapart, May 11, 2019. (French)</ref> appeared that same day and was followed rapidly by articles in [[Le Progrès]], [[Le Monde]], [[20 minutes (France)|20 minutes]], [[:fr:Lyon Capitale|Lyon Capitale]], [[:fr:LyonMag|Lyon Mag]], [[:fr:Le Figaro Étudiant|Le Figaro Étudiant]], 
[[Le Figaro]], [[Le Canard enchaîné]], [[:fr:Libération (journal)|Libération]], and [[L’Humanité]].<ref>''[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/SoutienTunaAltinel/#presse Survey of press with respect to the arrest of Tuna Altınel],'' support committee website, Lyon, accessed June 20, 2019</ref> Altınel was featured as L’Humanité's ''Man of the Day'' on May 16, 2019.  [[Euronews|Euronews TV]] reported on the case on May 30, 2019.<ref>Video: ''[https://fr.euronews.com/video/2019/05/30/soutien-a-un-universaitaire-turc-emprisonne Support for an imprisoned Turkish academic],'' Euronews, May 30, 2019; 2:20</ref>

====Official reactions====

Less than weeks after the confiscation of Altınel's passport, on April 23, 2019, the [[:fr:Société de mathématiques appliquées et industrielles|French Applied Mathematics Society]] and the [[:fr:Société mathématique de France|French Mathematical Society]] wrote jointly to President [[Emmanuel Macron|Macron of France]].<ref>
''[https://smf.emath.fr/sites/default/files/2019-04/19_04_22_Altinel_macron%20copie.pdf Letter to President Macron, April 23, 2019, from the Presidents of the French Mathematical Society and the Society for Applied and Industrial Mathematics (France)]'' (French)
</ref>

On May 11, the day of Altınel's arrest, the Turkish [[Consul (representative)#Consul General|Consul General]] in Lyon, Mehmet Özgür Çakar, stated "Tuna Altınel organized, and moderated, a meeting in Lyon consisting entirely of propaganda in favor of the PKK. ... It is possible that this had a negative effect on his situation."<ref>''[https://www.monde-diplomatique.fr/2016/07/A/55974 "President Erdoğan's dirty war: Thirty years of conflict"],'' in [[Le Monde diplomatique]], July 2016.</ref> The consul also noted that the PKK remains classified a terrorist group by Ankara, the [[United States]], and the [[European Union]].<ref>[http://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-actu/lyon-mobilisation-pour-un-universitaire-incarcere-en-turquie-20190514 ''Lyon: Movement in solidarity with an academic imprisoned in Turkey''], Le Figaro, May 14, 2019.</ref> The French [[:fr:Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires Etrangères|Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs]] expressed its "disquiet" on May 13, 2019.<ref>[https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/dossiers-pays/turquie/evenements/article/turquie-liberte-d-expression-13-05-19 "Turkey: Freedom of Speech"], French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs</ref> A support committee formed at Lyon created a website to document the evolution of the affair, and on May 23 the committee launched a petition in favor of the liberation of Altınel, with over 6000 signatories as of June, 2019, predominantly academics, along with approximately 60 members of the [[Parlement français|French National Assembly]].<ref>[https://math.univ-lyon1.fr/petitionTunaAltinel/ "Free Tuna Altinel," on-line petition]</ref>

Professional societies from a number of countries, including  mathematics societies in the United States, France, Great Britain, Germany Austria, Italy, and Belgium, as well as the [[European Mathematical Society]], the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]], and the [[Committee of Concerned Scientists]] have issued statements in support of Altınel.<ref>''[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/SoutienTunaAltinel/#officiel List of statements of support by professional institutions in support of Altinel];'' website of the support committee for Tuna Altınel, Lyon, accessed June 20, 2019.</ref>

====National Assembly, France====

On June 11, 2019, the French mathematician and politician [[Cédric Villani]] ([[:fr:en marche|LREM]]), [[:fr:Député français|Member of Parliament]] for [[:fr:cinquième circonscription de l'Essonne|Essonne's fifth district]] and [[Fields Medal|Fields medalist]], who is a colleague and an outspoken supporter of Altınel,<ref>[http://math.univ-lyon1.fr/SoutienTunaAltinel/doc/19_05_23_tweet_Villani.jpg Tweet, Cédric Villani, May 23, 2019]</ref> posed a question on the subject during a session of the National Assembly to the Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs [[Jean-Yves Le Drian]], who stated that the government was committed to doing "everything in its power" in favor of his liberation, notably on the occasion of his June 13 visit to Turkey to consult his counterpart there.<ref>''[http://www.lefigaro.fr/actualite-france/le-drian-assure-mettre-tout-en-oeuvre-pour-faire-liberer-en-turquie-un-professeur-de-lyon-20190611 Le Drian promises to make "every effort" to achieve the release of a professor from Lyon in Turkey,  Le Figaro, June 11, 2019]''; ''[https://france3-regions.francetvinfo.fr/auvergne-rhone-alpes/rhone/lyon/france-met-oeuvre-obtenir-liberation-mathematicien-turc-universite-lyon-1683940.html France is making “every effort” to achieve the release of a Turkish mathematician from the University of Lyon]'', on [[France 3 Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes|Local French television]], June 11, 2019.</ref>
